name: Big Daddy Kane
hook: A Brooklyn wordsmith who wrote rhymes for Biz Markie before writing his own, then spent a career being cited as the reason so many later MCs could rap fast and clean at once.
blurb: Antonio Hardy, born in Brooklyn in 1968, first wrote lyrics for his friend Biz Markie before joining Marley Marl's Juice Crew himself and signing to Cold Chillin' Records. His 1988 album 'Long Live the Kane' and its single 'Ain't No Half-Steppin'' showed off a fast, technically complex flow, with rhymes inside lines, breath control, and speed without losing clarity, that became a template for later rappers. He is one of the most cited technical influences of hip-hop's late-1980s generation; Rolling Stone has called him simply a huge influence on a generation of MCs. In the early 1990s, Kane brought an unknown Jay-Z on tour as his hype man and tried, unsuccessfully at the time, to get him a record deal. Jay-Z then appeared on Kane's 1994 track 'Show & Prove', one of the most directly documented cases of one MC's career opening a path for another.

signatureTracks.title: Ain't No Half-Steppin'
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Long Live the Kane'; Rolling Stone ranked it among the 50 greatest hip-hop songs ever made.

signatureTracks.title: Raw
